conviction_note: The company's own Q1 2026 release shows net profit fell 8.9% YoY (RMB98.4m vs RMB108.2m) on revenue +64.8% because sales and marketing tripled to 43.6% of revenue, and the Q2 comp (RMB140.2m) is 42% above the Q1 2026 run-rate; I net that against a near-certain September capital-return announcement (the US$50m buyback authorisation expires 2026-09-09, the day after the print, and the semi-annual dividend has been declared with the September release in both 2024 and 2025) and against a +5.7% five-day run-up that gives something to hand back, arriving at a modest negative just above this name's ~2.3% median reaction.

findings.finding: Waterdrop's Q1 2026 net profit FELL 8.9% year over year to RMB98.4m from RMB108.2m, and operating profit rose only 5.4% (RMB80.0m vs RMB75.9m) on revenue up 64.8%, because sales and marketing expense tripled — up 213.8% to RMB541.1m from RMB172.4m, or 43.6% of revenue — so the entire 'AI-driven growth' story is currently producing no incremental profit, and the Q2 2026 comparative is Q2 2025's RMB140.2m, 42% above the Q1 2026 run-rate.
findings.why_not_priced: The market's revealed reaction to this exact disclosure was POSITIVE: WDH closed +2.34% on the 2026-06-17 Q1 release (baseline reaction history), i.e. it traded the 'revenue +64.8% / insurance revenue +74.1%' headline and not the bottom line. There are no listed options on WDH, so there is no skew and no priced directional statement, and no sell-side model exists to publish an operating-margin bridge. If the profit trajectory (108.2 -> 140.2 -> 158.4 -> 162.1 in 2025, then 98.4 in Q1 2026) were priced, the stock would not be running +5.7% in the five sessions into the print off its 52-week low; you would see it drifting down into the date, and the June print would have been a down day, not a +2.3% day.
findings.independence: Corroborated from a different document: the FY2025 release of 2026-03-25 gives FY2025 net profit RMB568.9m and Q4 2025 RMB162.1m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1823986/000110465926034227/tm269697d1_ex99-1.htm), and the Q2 2025 release gives Q2 2025 net profit RMB140.2m on revenue RMB838.0m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1823986/000110465925087282/tm2524976d1_ex99-1.htm) — together fixing the 2025 quarterly profit path against which Q1 2026's RMB98.4m is a 39% sequential and 8.9% YoY decline. Separately, third-party commentary notes WDH 'has lost close to half its market cap in 2026, much of it very recently' (https://stockinvest.us/stock/WDH, data through 2026-08-18), which is consistent with the tape absorbing some of this — the reason my band extends to +0.8.

findings.finding: Waterdrop's current US$50m share repurchase authorisation runs 'during the 12-month period through September 9, 2026' — expiring the day AFTER this 2026-09-08 print — and it has been almost unused: cumulative repurchases went from approximately US$109.0m (55.7m ADSs) at 2025-08-31 to approximately US$120.1m (61.8m ADSs) at 2026-05-31, so roughly US$11m of the US$50m was spent in nine months; the company has launched a new programme every September for five straight years (2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025) and announced the 2025 one inside the Q2 earnings release itself, and its semi-annual dividend's second-half tranche has likewise been declared with the September release (ex-dates 2024-10-11 and 2025-10-10), where US$0.03 per ADS is now 2.86% of a US$1.0495 spot versus roughly 1.5% a year ago.
findings.why_not_priced: The 2026-09-09 expiry date exists only inside a twelve-month-old 6-K exhibit; no aggregator carries buyback authorisation expiries, and with no options market there is no vehicle in which anyone could have expressed a view on a one-day-later expiry. Yield trackers do show the dividend (dividend.com/stockanalysis show ~5.5%), so the dividend's EXISTENCE is priced — what is not re-marked anywhere is that the same absolute US$0.03 per ADS is now nearly twice its former size relative to a halved share price, and that the buyback has been dormant enough (approximately US$41k/day) that the 'large buyback' framing overstates any standing bid. If the September renewal were priced you would see the run-up concentrated in the days after 2026-08-25 when the date was announced rather than the broad +4.95% 20-day drift the baseline reports.
findings.independence: The dividend cadence is corroborated from a non-company source with dated ex-dividend records: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/wdh/dividend/ (retrieved 2026-09-04; ex-dates 2024-10-11, 2025-10-10, 2026-04-24). NOTE — this finding and the buyback-expiry fact share the 2025-09-04 6-K exhibit with nothing else in this file, and I have deliberately filed the buyback renewal and the dividend declaration as ONE finding rather than two, because they are one mechanism (Waterdrop's September capital-return announcement) and would otherwise be one fact counted twice.

findings.finding: China's eight financial and internet regulators jointly issued the Administrative Measures for Online Marketing of Financial Products on 2026-04-24, effective 2026-09-30 — 22 days after this print — whose Article 20 bars third-party internet platforms (defined as sites and apps 'not self-operated by a financial institution') from intervening or covertly intervening in sales-contract signing, fund transfer or suitability assessment, and from conducting interactive consultation with consumers about financial products, which puts a hard compliance date on the traffic architecture behind Waterdrop's insurance marketplace and its non-licensed Waterdrop Medical Crowdfunding funnel.
findings.why_not_priced: There is no English-language coverage connecting WDH to these Measures at all — searches for Waterdrop plus the rule return only the earnings-date press release. EDGAR full-text search for the Chinese term returns zero Waterdrop documents, so the FY2025 20-F filed 2026-04-28 (four days after issuance) does not name it. With no options and effectively no sell-side, there is no preview note in which a compliance date twenty-two days out could have been raised. If it were priced, the stock would have broken on 2026-04-24; instead the 2026-04/2026-06 tape shows no single-day dislocation and the June print was a positive reaction. I size it near zero and two-sided on purpose: the rule plausibly HELPS a licensed self-operated broker by forcing unlicensed traffic platforms to hand users off, which is Waterdrop's own model — the risk is that management is asked to quantify it on the 8:00 ET call and cannot.
findings.independence: Independently confirmed by Xinhua's report of the joint issuance, with 2026-04-24 in the URL path: https://www.news.cn/20260424/9c93b2c4f5194b7fbfe98fc4e51893ab/c.html . Directionally same-way corroboration from a separate regulatory strand — Chinese trade press reporting the 'bao-hang-he-yi' commission-unification tightening cutting intermediary channel commissions by more than 50% (https://m.10jqka.com.cn/20260331/c675657887.shtml, 2026-03-31).

findings.finding: Waterdrop turned over both of its finance-oversight seats in the five weeks immediately before this print: independent director Heping Feng left the board effective 2026-07-01 and was replaced by Qianfei Chang as independent director and audit committee chair (6-K, 2026-06-23), and then the vice president of finance and head of finance, Xiaoying Xu, resigned effective 2026-07-31 (6-K, 2026-07-24).
findings.why_not_priced: Each 6-K was filed alone and read alone; the finance exit has one derivative write-up and the board change another, and neither notes that the audit-committee chair and the head of finance both changed within thirty-eight days, with the second departure taking effect one month into the quarter now being reported. WDH closed +2.68% on 2026-07-24, the day the finance resignation was filed (baseline reaction history) — the market did not treat it as information. If it had been priced as a control-environment flag you would see a negative day on that filing and widening bid-ask, not a rally. I hold this small and partly-covered on purpose: the audit chair was named eight days before his predecessor left, which reads as an orderly refresh, not a rupture.
findings.independence: The board leg is a different document: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1823986/000110465926076631/tm2618547d1_ex99-1.htm (2026-06-23), with the audit-committee-chair role confirmed at https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/WDH/6-k-waterdrop-inc-current-report-foreign-issuer-10e66b9196d2.html . A third, genuinely odd strand points the same way and I could not explain it: eight Form 3s were filed for Waterdrop insiders in March 2026 — unusual because a foreign private issuer's insiders are exempt from Section 16 under Rule 3a12-3(b), and Waterdrop has continued to file 6-Ks and a 20-F rather than 10-Qs — including one for Haiyang Yu becoming a director on 2026-03-18 from Tencent Holdings' Hong Kong address at 29/F Three Pacific Place with no securities owned and no accompanying press release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1823986/000095010326004277/xslF345X06/ownership.xml). I flag it rather than score it because I could not establish what triggered it. NOTE: these two 6-Ks are ONE governance cluster and are filed here as one finding, not two.

baseline_tension: There is no skew or implied move to agree or disagree with, so the only priced statement is the run-up — and my largest finding cuts squarely against it: the stock is +5.7% in five sessions and +4.95% over twenty into a print whose most recent comparable disclosure showed profit falling year over year while marketing spend tripled, and my one positive finding (the September capital-return ritual) is the part of the run-up that may already be someone else's trade.
